- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (positive sentiment > 0.0) — model tends to overshoot, especially after recent spikes.
- Underestimate prices in bearish sentiment (negative sentiment < -0.3) — model shows persistent downward bias, often failing to capture early reversal.
- Lag in downward corrections: model delays price drops, especially when sentiment turns negative — true price falls faster than forecast.
- Mean reversion bias: model overreacts to short-term volatility, overcorrecting after sharp moves — prices often revert to prior mean faster than model suggests.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts consistently overestimate early in the period (first 5–7 days) and underestimate late (last 5–7 days) — model “peaks too early” and “bottoms too late.”
- Sentiment-weighted adjustment: if sentiment is > 0.1, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overconfidence; if sentiment < -0.3, increase forecast by 5–10% to counteract pessimism.
